title: Roll, the whole game: three boards, crates to push, a moving bridge, a menu, saved settings, two languages
brief: Build a game called Roll. It is in three dimensions.
The ball and the boards
- Lengths are in metres, y is up. A board is a flat slab 0.2 thick with its top face at y = 0 and no walls. Gravity is 9.81 m/s2.

- The ball has radius 0.25 and mass 1 kg. It is a rigid body: it rolls, bounces at least once when it lands (each bounce lower than the one before), keeps moving when a push ends and slows only gently, and falls when it leaves an edge. At the start of a board it is at rest at that board's start.
- The player pushes the ball: Right (D) toward +x, Left (A) toward -x, Up (W) toward -z (away from the camera), Down (S) toward +z. A push accelerates the ball by 4 m/s2 for as long as it is held.

- The ball takes a coin when its centre comes within 0.5 of the coin's: 10 points, the coin is gone, the sound `coin` plays. A board is cleared when its last coin is taken; the next board then begins (the sound `clear` plays), and the run is won when board 3 is cleared.

- A ball whose centre drops below y = -5 has fallen: one of 3 lives is lost (the lives are for the whole run, not for a board), the sound `fall` plays, the ball is put back at rest at the board's start, and everything else on the board is as it was (coins taken stay taken; crates stay where they are; a crate that has itself fallen below y = -5 is gone). The run is lost when the third life is lost.
- Each time the ball lands on a board or on the bridge at more than 1 m/s the sound `bounce` plays.
The three boards
- Board 1: one slab, x from -3 to 3 and z from -3 to 3. The ball starts at (0, 1.25, 0). Coins at (2, 0.25, 0), (-2, 0.25, 0), (0, 0.25, 2), (0, 0.25, -2).

- Board 2: one slab, x from -4 to 4 and z from -2 to 2. The ball starts at (-3, 1.25, 0). Six crates stand as a wall across the board at x = 0: cubes 0.5 on a side of 0.5 kg each, two high and three across, centred at z = -0.5, 0 and 0.5 and at y = 0.25 and 0.75. They are rigid bodies: the ball pushes and topples them, they fall, slide and push one another, and they can be pushed off the board. Coins at (-1.5, 0.25, 1.5), (1.5, 0.25, 0) and (3, 0.25, -1).

- Board 3: two slabs with a gap between them. The first has x from -5 to -1 and z from -1.5 to 1.5; the second x from 3 to 7 and z from -1.5 to 1.5. A bridge, a slab 2 long in x, 2 deep in z (from -1 to 1) and 0.2 thick with its top at y = 0, slides along x across the gap and back without end: its centre goes from x = 0 to x = 2 in 3 seconds at a steady speed, then back in 3 seconds, starting at x = 0 moving toward +x when the board begins. It carries the ball: a ball at rest on the bridge moves with it. The ball starts at (-4, 1.25, 0). Coins at (-2, 0.25, 0), (1, 0.25, 0) (over the gap: taken from the bridge) and (5, 0.25, 0).
The screens
- Title: the game's name and three choices: Start, Settings, Quit (Up / Down move, Enter chooses).
- Settings: Volume (0 to 10, Left / Right change it, 8 at first), Language (English or Spanish, Left / Right change it, English at first) and Back. Both are kept between runs of the game.
- Play: the board, with the board's number as "Board 1 of 3", the score and the lives left. Escape pauses ("Paused", with Resume and Quit to title); nothing moves while paused.
- Won and Lost: "You win" or "Game over", the score, and Enter to go back to the title.
- Every word on every screen is in the chosen language.

- The view of a board is in perspective: a camera above and in front of the board (on the +z side, looking down at it), far enough to show the whole board, with light and shade that show the ball is round and the crates are boxes.
- The game advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second. What happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn, and the same inputs at the same ticks always give the same game.
- The four sounds (`coin`, `bounce`, `fall`, `clear`) are the game's own, each under a second, each told from the others by ear, and played at the volume the setting gives (silent at 0).
Checkable without hands
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer three things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a number of ticks, a script of inputs (at tick T one word: left, right, up, down, none for the pushes, which hold until the next one; enter, escape, menu_up, menu_down, menu_left, menu_right, each pressed once at that tick), an optional board to start on (1, 2 or 3: the run then starts in play on that board, with score 0 and 3 lives, as if the boards before it had been cleared without scoring) and an optional folder where settings are kept, it runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick", "screen" (title, settings, play, paused, won, lost), "board", "score", "lives", "ball": {"x", "y", "z"}, "coins": [{"x", "z"}] (not yet taken, this board), "crates": [{"x", "y", "z"}] (board 2: the crates still there, their centres), "bridge_x" (board 3: the bridge's centre), "volume", "language" (en, es), "selected" (the menu choice in focus, as its English word), "texts": [..] (every text on the screen, as shown), "sounds": [..] (every sound played so far, in order)}. Keys that mean nothing on a screen or a board may be null.
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 800 pixels wide and 480 tall.
3. Each sound as a WAV file: either the files themselves in the work folder, or the exact command that writes one.
Hand in, in your work folder
- The game, ready to run.
- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the three checks, how the game is put together (which file holds what), and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, takes a tick count, an input script, an optional starting board and an optional settings folder, and prints the state as the brief's JSON object.
The frame is written as an 800 x 480 PNG after a headless run.
Each of the four sounds (coin, bounce, fall, clear) can be had as a WAV file by what the README says; each is under a second, not silent, and no two are the same sound.
The game opens on the title with Start in focus; menu_down and menu_up move the focus through Start, Settings and Quit; enter on Start begins play on board 1 with score 0 and 3 lives.
Settings shows Volume 8 and English at first; menu_left and menu_right change the volume by 1 within 0 to 10 and switch the language; Back returns to the title.
With Spanish chosen, every text on the title, settings, play, paused, won and lost screens is Spanish (none left in English, none missing), the board's number included.
Volume and language are kept: a second headless run with the same settings folder starts with what the first one set; without a settings folder a run starts at 8 and English.

In play with no input on board 1 the ball falls, first reaches the board (y at or below 0.3) between tick 20 and tick 40 of play, bounces (its y goes back above 0.3) and after 600 ticks rests with y within 0.05 of 0.25; `bounce` is in `sounds`, no more than 6 times.
The pushes move the ball as the brief says (right +x, left -x, up -z, down +z), and after a push ends on a board the ball keeps moving the same way for at least 30 more ticks.

A coin taken adds exactly 10 points, leaves `coins` and adds `coin` to `sounds`; when board 1's fourth coin is taken `board` becomes 2, `clear` is added to `sounds`, and the ball is at rest at board 2's start with board 2's coins and six crates in the state.
On board 2 with no input the six crates stand where the brief puts them and stay there for 300 ticks (each within 0.05 of its place: they neither sink, drift nor fall over on their own).

On board 2 a ball pushed right from its start strikes the wall of crates: at least two crates end more than 0.3 from where they stood, the ball is slowed by it (it arrives later at x = 1 than it would on an empty board, or does not arrive), and no crate passes through the board (none rests with y below 0.2 while still over the board).
A crate pushed off the board's edge falls, and once below y = -5 it is no longer in `crates`; the others remain.

A fall costs one life, adds `fall` to `sounds` and puts the ball back at rest at the board's start, with the coins taken and the crates as they were; the lives are counted over the whole run (a life lost on board 1 is still lost on board 2).
On board 3 with no input `bridge_x` goes from 0 to 2 in 180 ticks and back to 0 in the next 180, without end (within 0.05 at ticks 90, 180, 270 and 360 of the board: 1, 2, 1, 0).

On board 3 a ball that has come to rest on the bridge is carried by it: with no input its x follows `bridge_x` (within 0.3 over 180 ticks) and it does not fall through or slide off; a ball pushed right off the first slab while the bridge is away falls into the gap.

There is a script that clears board 3 started with the board option (its three coins, the one over the gap from the bridge): `screen` becomes won, `score` is 30 for that run, and further ticks change nothing until enter returns to the title.
After the third life is lost `screen` is lost, and further ticks and pushes change neither the score, the ball, the coins nor the crates; enter returns to the title.
Escape in play pauses: the screen is paused, and no tick changes the ball, the crates, the bridge or the score until Resume; Quit to title returns to the title.
Two headless runs with the same ticks, script, board and settings print identical states (the crates' places on board 2 after a strike included).

The frame of board 2 in play is a view in perspective from above and in front that shows the whole board, the ball where the state puts it and shaded as a round thing, each crate where the state puts it and drawn as a box with shaded faces, and the coins not yet taken; the frame of board 3 shows the two slabs, the gap and the bridge where `bridge_x` puts it.
The frames of the title, settings, paused, won and lost screens show their texts in the chosen language; the play frame shows the board's number, the score and the lives left.
At volume 0 the game plays no sound a player would hear, and the README or the code shows where the volume setting scales what is played (`sounds` in the state still lists them).
README.md says how to play, gives commands for the three checks that work as written, and says which file holds what.
